title: KnownValueSmoothConvexLocalLinear.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a differentiable convex objective over a nonempty closed convex set C in a real Hilbert space. On C, f satisfies the quadratic upper model with public L > 0. A minimizer xstar exists with ‖x0 − xstar‖ ≤ R.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: At each feasible query x, the oracle returns the exact gradient ∇f(x), for every call index and seed.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same feasible-point query returns the exact value f(x) together with its gradient.

oracle.label: linear_minimization
oracle.details: For feasible x, any r ≥ 0, and any direction g, return an exact minimizer of ⟨g,v⟩ over v ∈ C with ‖v − x‖ ≤ r. Value-gradient queries and local linear-minimization queries share one fixed budget of 3(⌈√(10LR²/ε)⌉ + 1) calls.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/KnownValueSmoothConvexLocalLinear.lean: spec.admissible, .inr oracle condition; supplied OracleTemplate.SplitBrox.result budget; LongTails/Template.lean: execute.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public information comprises the real Hilbert space, L > 0, R ≥ 0, ε > 0, feasible x0, and the exact optimum value fstar. The objective f and constraint set C are hidden. The set may be unbounded; R bounds distance to one minimizer rather than the diameter of C. Smoothness inequalities are required only for pairs in C. Local linear minimizers must exist for every admissible query; no oracle-error or independence assumption is needed.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a feasible point output ∈ C satisfying f(output) − f(xstar) ≤ ε, where xstar minimizes f on C and f(xstar) = fstar.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the objective-gap bound hold almost surely under the joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed probability measure, after the fixed oracle budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Smooth constrained convex optimization is classical, but exact access to linear minimization over arbitrary local ball intersections, combined with a publicly known optimum value and Hilbert-space geometry, defines a specialized oracle formulation. No repository implementation or proof was inspected; the literature search does not certify novelty.

descriptionHtml:
Known-Value Convex Local Linear Optimization

We consider minimizing f:E→R over a closed convex set C in a real Hilbert space E. On C, the function is differentiable and convex with a quadratic upper model of curvature L>0. A given x0∈C is within distance R≥0 of a minimizer with known value f⋆∈R. The oracle returns either a function value and gradient or a local linear minimizer over a queried ball intersected with C. For ε>0, the goal is x¯∈C with f(x¯)−f⋆≤ε almost surely under P, the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Cf(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ on E. The algorithm receives E, L, R, ε, f⋆, and x0; the objective and feasible set are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasible set). The set C⊆E is closed and convex, and x0∈C.

Assumption 2 (Convexity and quadratic upper model). The function f is Fréchet differentiable at every point of C. For every x,y∈C, f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩,f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+L2∥y−x∥2.

Assumption 3 (Known minimum and initial distance). There exists x⋆∈C such that f(x⋆)=f⋆,f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈C,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

The oracle supports two types of queries. At x∈C, a value–gradient query returns (f(x),∇f(x)). A local linear query specifies x∈C, a radius r≥0, and a direction g∈E, and returns a point v∈argminz∈C, ∥z−x∥≤r⁡⟨g,z⟩. Such a point must exist for every valid local linear query. The oracle may choose among these minimizers using the query history and its randomness, but every reply must satisfy the stated requirement. Both query types count toward a single total oracle-call budget.

After the allotted calls, the output must satisfy x¯∈C,f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s. The algorithm’s randomness is independent of the oracle’s randomness in the joint law P.

theorems.formulaHtml: 3⋅(⌈10⋅L⋅R2ε⌉++1)

comparisonHtml:
A real Hilbert space, a closed convex set C, and x0∈C. The differentiable objective satisfies 0≤f(y)−f(x)−⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩≤(L/2)∥y−x∥2 for x,y∈C. Known inputs are L>0, R≥0, ε>0, and f⋆=f(x⋆) for a minimizer x⋆∈C with ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. Exact oracles return (f(x),∇f(x)) and a minimizer of ⟨g,v⟩ over v∈C∩B(x,r). Target: feasible y with f(y)−f(x⋆)≤ε; (1) guarantees its last primal iterate for every seed and oracle tie-breaking choice.

Known-value convex optimization with exact local linear minimization: KnownValueSmoothConvexLocalLinear.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) SplitBroxKnownValue (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+LR2/ε) total value-gradient and local-LMO calls, including all trials.
(2) BroxGD (Richtárik et al. 2026, Thm. 3.2(ii), Cor. D.2) O(1+LR2/ε) total value-gradient and local-LMO calls. Finite-dimensional; R>0; L-Lipschitz gradient on an open convex neighborhood of C. (1): factor LR2/ε fewer calls when LR2/ε≥1; last instead of best iterate. Scope: quadratic models only on C suffice. (1) needs exact f⋆ and L additionally; (2) uses only R,K to set radii.
(3) Polyak-radius BroxGD (Richtárik et al. 2026, Thm. 3.5, Eq. (24)) O(1+(∥∇f(x⋆)∥+LR)2R2ε2) total value-gradient and local-LMO calls. Finite-dimensional; smooth on an open neighborhood of C; known f⋆. (1): ε−1/2 instead of ε−2 in this general guarantee, without ∥∇f(x⋆)∥ dependence; last instead of averaged iterate. (1) needs L,R additionally.
(4) APMM (Deng et al. 2026, Alg. 1, Thm. 2.1); ρ=1, Xk=C, no functional constraints O(1+LR2/ε) total value-gradient evaluations and exact projections onto C∩{ℓf≤f⋆}. Finite-dimensional smooth case. (1) matches the accelerated order using point-only local LMOs, with no logarithmic search overhead. Different oracles prevent a direct cost comparison. (1) needs L,R additionally; (4) is parameter-free apart from f⋆,ε.
(5) CGS (Lan and Zhou 2016, Cor. 3, 2014 preprint); special case: bounded C⊆Rd of diameter D O(1+LD2/ε) total gradient and global-LMO calls; gradient calls alone: O(1+LD2/ε). (1): for R≤D and LD2/ε≥1, at least a factor LD2/ε fewer linear-oracle calls. Scope: unbounded C allowed. (1) needs f⋆ and the stronger local LMO; (5) needs only global linear minimization over C.

Abbr: LMO: linear minimization oracle; local LMO: one point minimizing a linear function on C∩B(x,r); B(x,r): closed ball; D=supx,y∈C∥x−y∥; K: iteration horizon; ℓf(v;z)=f(z)+⟨∇f(z),v−z⟩. Costs count each oracle invocation once.

Deng, Qi, Guanghui Lan, and Zhenwei Lin. 2026. Uniformly Optimal and Parameter-Free First-Order Methods for Convex and Function-Constrained Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2412.06319.
Lan, Guanghui, and Yi Zhou. 2016. “Conditional Gradient Sliding for Convex Optimization.” SIAM Journal on Optimization 26 (2): 1379–409. https://doi.org/10.1137/140992382.
Richtárik, Peter, Kaja Gruntkowska, and Hanmin Li. 2026. Broximal Gradient Descent: A Projection-Free Sister of Projected Gradient Descent. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2605.08850.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function

namespace OracleTemplate.SplitBrox

abbrev Query (E : Type*) := E ⊕ (E × ℝ × E)

abbrev Reply (E : Type*) := (ℝ × E) ⊕ E

end OracleTemplate.SplitBrox

open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.KnownValueSmoothConvexLocalLinear

open OracleTemplate OracleTemplate.SplitBrox

structure Public where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  fstar : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  C : Set p.E

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Public
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := Query p.E
  Reply p := Reply p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I O :=
    Convex ℝ I.C ∧ IsClosed I.C ∧ p.x0 ∈ I.C ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, HasGradientAt I.f (gradient I.f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, ∀ y ∈ I.C, I.f x + ⟪gradient I.f x, y - x⟫ ≤ I.f y) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, ∀ y ∈ I.C,
      I.f y ≤ I.f x + ⟪gradient I.f x, y - x⟫ + p.L / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ k seed x, x ∈ I.C → O.answer k (0, .inl x) seed =
      .inl (I.f x, gradient I.f x)) ∧
    (∀ k seed x r g, x ∈ I.C → 0 ≤ r →
      ∃ v ∈ I.C, ‖v - x‖ ≤ r ∧
        (∀ z ∈ I.C, ‖z - x‖ ≤ r → ⟪g, v⟫ ≤ ⟪g, z⟫) ∧
        O.answer k (0, .inr (x, r, g)) seed = .inr v) ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ I.C, IsMinOn I.f I.C xstar ∧ I.f xstar = p.fstar ∧
      ‖p.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ p.R)
  successful p I output P :=
    ∃ xstar ∈ I.C, IsMinOn I.f I.C xstar ∧ I.f xstar = p.fstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), output ω ∈ I.C ∧ I.f (output ω) - I.f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.KnownValueSmoothConvexLocalLinear
